ing: seeds removed for less heat, or habanero
st: Wear gloves to handle the scotch bonnet. Blend it with the scallions, thyme, allspice, garlic, soy sauce, lime juice, sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, oil, salt and pepper into a thick paste.
Cut two or three deep slashes in each piece of chicken so the marinade can get in.
Rub the paste all over and under the skin. Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
Heat a grill to medium, or heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) with a rack in the middle.
Grill skin side down for 8 minutes, then flip and cook with the lid closed. In the oven, bake on a rack over a sheet pan.
Cook for another 30 to 35 minutes, turning now and then, until the chicken is charred in spots and reads 165°F (74°C) at the thickest part.
Move to a plate, tent with foil and rest for 10 minutes.
Serve with rice and peas, festival or bread, and wash your hands well after handling the peppers.
Soak the salt cod in cold water for 4 hours or overnight, changing the water twice.
Drain, then boil the cod in fresh water for 15 minutes. Drain, cool and flake it, removing any bones.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4 minutes.
Add the scallions, bell pepper, scotch bonnet and thyme and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 4 minutes until softened.
Add the flaked cod and black pepper. Stir for 2 minutes.
Fold in the ackee very gently, as it breaks up easily. Cover and cook for 5 minutes.
Remove the thyme stems and serve hot with fried dumplings, boiled green banana, or breadfruit.

ing: bone-in, cut into chunks, or lamb shoulder
st: Season the goat with [[2 tbsp]] curry powder, the salt, pepper, allspice, half the garlic and half the scallions. Marinate for at least 1 hour.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the remaining [[1 tbsp]] curry powder and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the goat in batches and brown for 10 minutes in total.
Add the onion, remaining garlic and thyme and cook for 4 minutes.
Pour in the water to nearly cover the meat. Add the whole scotch bonnet. Do not burst it.
Cover and simmer on low for 1.5 hours, stirring now and then, until the goat is almost tender.
Add the potatoes and simmer for 25 minutes until they are soft and the gravy has thickened.
Discard the scotch bonnet and thyme stems. Top with the remaining scallions and serve with rice and peas.
Season the oxtail with the soy sauce, browning sauce, allspice, salt, pepper and half the garlic. Marinate for at least 1 hour.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the oxtail in batches for 12 minutes in total. Set aside.
Cook the onion, scallions and remaining garlic in the same pot for 4 minutes.
Return the oxtail and add the thyme, scotch bonnet and enough water to cover.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 2.5 hours until the meat is tender.
Add the carrots and cook for 20 minutes.
Add the butter beans and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until the gravy is thick.
Discard the scotch bonnet and thyme stems. Serve with rice and peas.
Drain the kidney beans, saving their liquid, and set the beans aside.
In a pot, combine the bean liquid, coconut milk, water, scallions, thyme, garlic, allspice, scotch bonnet, salt and pepper. Bring to a boil.
Add the beans and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the rinsed rice. The liquid should be about 1 inch above the rice. Add water if needed.
Bring back to a boil, then reduce to the lowest heat and cover tightly.
Cook for 20 to 25 minutes without lifting the lid until the rice is tender.
Rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Remove the thyme stems, scallions and scotch bonnet. Fluff with a fork and serve.
Mix the flour, turmeric and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Rub in the cold butter until it looks like coarse crumbs with some pea-size pieces.
Add the ice water a spoonful at a time until the dough just holds together. Shape into a disc, wrap, and chill for 1 hour.
Heat the oil in a pan. Cook the onion for 4 minutes, then add the garlic, curry powder, thyme and scotch bonnet for 1 minute.
Add the beef and [[0.5 tsp]] salt and cook for 8 minutes until browned and cooked through at 160°F (71°C).
Stir in the broth and bread crumbs and simmer for 5 minutes until moist, not wet. Cool completely.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Roll the dough out to 1/8 inch thick and cut into eight 6 inch circles.
Put [[3 tbsp]] filling on one half of each circle, brush the edge with egg, fold over, and crimp with a fork.
Place on a lined sheet, brush with egg, and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until golden. Cool for 5 minutes before eating.

ing: cleaned and scored, or fish fillets
st: Season the fish with [[1 tsp]] salt and the black pepper, inside and out. Let it sit for 15 minutes.
For the pickle, simmer the vinegar, water, allspice, sugar and [[0.5 tsp]] salt for 3 minutes.
Add the onion, carrot, bell pepper and scotch bonnet and cook for 2 minutes. They should stay crunchy. Set aside.
Dry the fish well, then dredge in the flour and shake off the excess.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering at about 350°F (175°C).
Fry the fish for 5 to 6 minutes per side until golden and crisp. The flesh should reach 145°F (63°C).
Drain on paper towels and move to a deep dish.
Spoon the hot pickled vegetables and liquid over the fish. Serve warm or let it marinate for 30 minutes or overnight.
Whisk the flour, cornmeal, sugar, baking powder, salt and nutmeg in a bowl.
Add the vanilla to the milk, then stir it in a little at a time until a soft, firm dough forms.
Knead briefly for 2 minutes until smooth. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 pieces and roll each into a log about 5 inches long, with tapered ends.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the festivals in batches for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until deep golden brown and cooked through.
Drain the festivals on paper towels for a few minutes.
Serve warm with jerk chicken or fried fish.

ing: or finely grated and squeezed cassava
st: Mix the cassava flour and salt in a bowl.
Add the warm water a spoonful at a time until the mixture clumps like damp sand.
Let it rest for 10 minutes so the flour absorbs the water.
Divide into 4 portions and press each into a flat round about 1/2 inch thick, using wet hands.
Heat a dry nonstick pan over medium heat and cook each round for 4 minutes per side until firm and lightly colored.
Soak the bammy in the coconut milk for 5 minutes on each side.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and fry the bammy for 3 minutes per side until golden.
Serve hot with butter, alongside fried fish or ackee.
Wear gloves and wash your hands well afterward, as scotch bonnets are very hot.
Put the peppers, scallions, garlic and ginger in a blender.
Add the allspice, thyme, soy sauce, lime juice, sugar, oil, cinnamon, black pepper and salt.
Blend for 1 minute into a thick, slightly chunky paste.
Taste a tiny amount and add more salt or lime to balance the heat.
Use right away as a marinade for chicken, pork or fish, or store in a jar in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.
Mix the flour and salt. Rub in the butter until it looks like coarse crumbs.
Stir in the ice water a spoonful at a time until a dough forms. Chill for 30 minutes.
For the filling, simmer the coconut, brown sugar, water, nutmeg and ginger over medium-low heat for 10 minutes, stirring, until the mixture is sticky and thick.
Stir in the vanilla and cool.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Roll the dough 1/8 inch thick and cut 3 inch circles.
Press each circle into a muffin tin cup, then pinch the edge in a ruffle to form a tart shell. Prick the bottom with a fork.
Bake the empty shells for 10 minutes, then fill each with [[1 tbsp]] of filling.
Bake for 10 minutes more until the shells are golden. Cool before serving.

ing: optional, or leave it out for a non-alcoholic drink
st: Rinse the sorrel in cold water to remove dust.
Put the sorrel, ginger, cloves, cinnamon, allspice and orange peel in a large pot.
Add the water and bring to a boil.
Turn off the heat, cover, and steep for 8 hours or overnight, at room temperature.
Strain through a fine sieve into a pitcher, pressing the flowers to get all the color out.
Stir in the sugar until dissolved, tasting as you go to get it sweet enough.
Add the rum now if you like, or skip it.
Chill and serve over ice.
Rinse [[1 cup]] dried Irish moss well under cold water to remove sand. Soak in a bowl of water for 30 minutes.
Drain and put in a pot with [[3 cup]] fresh water. Simmer on low for 15 minutes until the moss turns soft and the water looks gel-like.
Transfer moss and cooking liquid to a blender. Add [[1 cup]] more water and blend for 1 minute until smooth.
Add [[0.5 cup]] condensed milk, [[1 cup]] evaporated milk, [[0.5 tsp]] nutmeg and [[1 tsp]] vanilla. Blend 30 seconds more.
Strain through a sieve into a jug and chill. It thickens as it cools. Serve over ice, with extra nutmeg sprinkled on top.
nt: Simmered until gel, then blended cold
Best swap: use coconut milk and maple syrup in place of the two milks for a vegan version.

st: Mix the chicken with the onion, scallions, thyme, garlic, allspice, [[1 tbsp]] soy sauce and salt. Marinate at least 1 hour in the fridge.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil with [[1 tbsp]] brown sugar in a heavy pot over medium heat for 2 minutes until it bubbles and turns dark amber.
Lift the chicken from the marinade, shaking off the bits, and brown in the caramel for 4 minutes per side. Do not crowd the pot.
Add the marinade vegetables, carrot, [[1 tbsp]] ketchup, [[1 tbsp]] soy sauce and [[1.5 cup]] water. Float the whole pepper on top.
Cover and braise over low heat for 35 minutes until the chicken reads 175°F and the gravy is dark and thick.
Remove the pepper and serve with rice and peas.
nt: Browned in caramelized sugar, then braised
Best swap: use a habanero in place of Scotch bonnet. Leave it whole for flavor and mild heat.
